newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dollar/yen vols soar as spot crumbles.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/yen vols soar as spot crumbles.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/yen options shot up as the spot rate crashed more than three yen from its overnight highs to hit a five-month low in Europe.
One-month dollar/yen vols were at 14.00/14.50 percent at 0945 GMT against 11.80/12.10 in late European trade on Monday.

"Dollar/yen vols are where all the action is today...since generally as dollar/yen moves down, volatility spikes up and when the spot reverses upward, vols ease off," said James Binney, fund manager at GNI in London.
Yen call demand heightened, with one-month 25-delta risk reversals at 1.4/1.9 percent for yen calls against 1.0/1.4 on Monday.

Speculation of an interest rate rise in Japan in the near future re-emerged overnight to drive dollar/yen lower, sparked by a report that a committee of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party was considering asking for a rise in the key discount rate.
An LDP official said the committee has not decided whether to request the rate hike. Later, a senior party official was quoted as saying now was not the time to tighten credit policy.
Dollar/yen dropped to 111.98 yen in morning Europe, its lowest since December 6 last year, from 115.93/03 in late Europe on Monday. It had recovered to 113.66/76 by midday.
"People are waiting for the FOMC, but for now they're being spot-driven, looking more at what's happening in Japan," GNI's Binney said.
The Federal Reserve is due to hold its policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting later today, with the market split on whether it will decide to raise rates.

Meanwhile, mark/yen's continued slide to a 20-month low of 66.43 yen earlier also boosted mark/yen vols, with one-month vol rising to 11.20/11.70 percent from Monday's 10.10/10.60. Risk reversals still favoured mark puts at 1.0/1.3 against 0.7/1.0.
Traders said the strength in dollar/yen volatilities was helping to spur activity in mark/yen vols.
Spot mark/yen had recovered to near 67 yen by midday, but was still far below late Monday's 67.85/90.

Dollar/mark vols firmed but were largely sidelined as moves in the spot rate were less spectacular than in dollar/yen and the cross. One-month vols climbed to 9.80/10.10 from Monday's 9.25/9.55 and risk reversals, skewed towards mark calls, were at 0.2/0.5 against 0.15/45.
